This notebook describes the first example in the numerical experiments section of the paper REF.

# Data Generation

We generate data according to the Fokker-Plank-Kolmogorov equation of example REF, i.e., with $X_{t+1} = X_{t} + \theta_1 + \theta_2 X_t + \theta_3 Z_t$ and with $X_1 \sim N(-10,1)$. Each dataset will consist of 20 time points with varying sample sizes of $n_t = 100, 300, 900, 3000, 10000$, and we will replicate 100 draws for each sample size and parameter values. 


```{r}
forwards_FPK_model <- function( m_alpha, l_data, kde_inds, m_covariates = NULL ) {
  times <- names(l_data)
  result <- Map(
    function(x, idx) {
      x[idx] + m_alpha[1] + m_alpha[2] * x[idx] + m_alpha[3] * array(rnorm(length(x[idx])), dim = dim(x[idx]))
    },
    l_data,
    kde_inds[times]
  )
  nms <- names(result)[-1]
  result <- result[-length(result)]
  names(result) <- nms
  
  first_item <- list(NULL)
  names(first_item) <- times[1]

  return( append(result, first_item, after = 0 ) )
}
```

```{r}
generate_FPK_data <- function( num_times, num_samples, m_alpha ) {
  X <- matrix( rnorm(num_times * num_samples, mean = -10) , nrow = num_times, ncol = num_samples )
  for (i in 2:num_times) {
    X_temp <- X[i:num_times, , drop = FALSE]
    Z_t <- array(rnorm(length(X_temp)), dim = dim(X_temp))
    X[i:num_times,] <- X_temp + m_alpha[1] + m_alpha[2] * X_temp + m_alpha[3] * Z_t
  }
  return( setNames( asplit(X, 1), paste0("row", seq_len(nrow(X))) ) )
}
```

```{r}
num_replicates <- 100
num_times <- 20
num_samples <- c(100, 300, 900, 3000, 10000)
m_alpha <- c(1,0,0)
datasets <- vector("list", length(num_samples)) 

for (i in 1:length(num_samples)) {
  n_samps <- num_samples[i]
  datasets[[i]] <- vector("list", num_replicates)
  for (j in 1:num_replicates) {
    datasets[[i]][[j]] <- generate_FPK_data( num_times, n_samps, m_alpha ) 
  }
}
```


# Fitting aMLEs

We fit the parameters in the model using the approximate maximum likelihood estimator (aMLE) using the code in the accompanying package.

```{r, cache = TRUE}
n_par <- 3

mles <- vector("list", length(num_samples))
for (i in 1:length(num_samples)) {
  mles[[i]] <- vector("list", num_replicates)
  for (j in 1:num_replicates) {
    mles[[i]][[j]] <- fit_theta_one_step_forw_list( datasets[[i]][[j]], 
                                                    forwards_FPK_model, 
                                                    n_par, 
                                                    plot_flag = FALSE, 
                                                    trace_lvl = 0 ) 
  }
}
```


```{r}
par_list <- lapply(mles, function(x) {
  lapply(x, function(y) y$par)
})
```

```{r}
df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(par_list), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    i = i,
    samp_size = num_samples[i],
    par1 = sapply(par_list[[i]], function(y) y[1]), 
    par2 = sapply(par_list[[i]], function(y) y[2]), 
    par3 = sapply(par_list[[i]], function(y) y[3])
  )
}))

df_long <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(par1, par2, par3),
    names_to = "parameter",
    values_to = "estimate"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    parameter = factor(
      parameter,
      levels = c("par1", "par2", "par3"),
      labels = c("theta[1]", "theta[2]", "theta[3]")  # plotmath syntax for facet labels
    )
  )

ggplot(df_long, aes(x = factor(samp_size), y = estimate)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ parameter, labeller = label_parsed, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = expression("Sample Size (" * n[t] * ")"),
    y = "Estimate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

From this plot we can see that the parameter values converge in towards their true values. 

# Hypothesis Testing

We now test the hypotheses $H_0 : \theta = (1,0,0)$ and the incorrect hypothesis $H_1 : \theta = (0.98, 0.01, 0.01)$ accross these simulated datasets. 

```{r, cache = TRUE}
m_theta_ranges_H_0 <- list(
  theta1 = c(1),
  theta2 = c(0),
  theta3 = c(0)
)
m_theta_ranges_H_1 <- list(
  theta1 = c(0.98),
  theta2 = c(0.01),
  theta3 = c(0.01)
)

p_vals_H_0 <- vector("list", length(num_samples))
p_vals_H_1 <- vector("list", length(num_samples))
for (i in 1:length(num_samples)) {
  p_vals_H_0[[i]] <- vector("list", num_replicates)
  p_vals_H_1[[i]] <- vector("list", num_replicates)
  for (j in 1:num_replicates) {
    p_vals_H_0[[i]][[j]] <- fit_CR_KS_list( datasets[[i]][[j]], 
                                            forwards_FPK_model, 
                                            m_theta_ranges_H_0, 
                                            NULL, 
                                            plot_flag = FALSE )
    p_vals_H_1[[i]][[j]] <- fit_CR_KS_list( datasets[[i]][[j]], 
                                            forwards_FPK_model, 
                                            m_theta_ranges_H_1, 
                                            NULL, 
                                            plot_flag = FALSE )
  }
}
```

```{r}
alpha <- 0.05

make_prop_plot <- function(pvals_list, title_expr = NULL) {
  prop_df <- data.frame(
    i = seq_along(pvals_list),
    prop_below = sapply(pvals_list, function(x) {
      vals <- sapply(x, function(y) y$ks_fisher_p_vals)
      mean(vals < alpha)
    })
  )

  ggplot(prop_df, aes(x = factor(num_samples[i]), y = prop_below)) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = alpha, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
    ggtitle(title_expr) +
    labs(
      x = expression("Sample Size (" * n[t] * ")"),
      y = expression("Proportion below " * alpha)
    ) +
    ylim(0, 1) +
    theme_minimal()
}

p1 <- make_prop_plot(p_vals_H_0, title_expr = expression("Under " * H[0]))
p2 <- make_prop_plot(p_vals_H_1, title_expr = expression("Under " * H[1]))

p1 + p2
```
We see that the true hypothesis is accepted at the correct empirical level and the that test has power against the incorrect hypothesis and this power converges to 1 for this scenario. Note that this also means that the confidence regions contain the true parameter values at the appropriate level because the only way to fail this is to reject $H_0$. 

# Confidence Regions

Lastly we consider confidence regions for one of the datasets with $n_t = 300$.

```{r, cache = TRUE}
m_theta_ranges <- list(
  theta1 = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.2),
  theta2 = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.2),
  theta3 = seq(-2, 2, by = 0.2)
)

l_data <- datasets[[2]][[1]]

sim_cr <- fit_CR_KS_list( l_data, 
                          forwards_FPK_model, 
                          m_theta_ranges, 
                          NULL, 
                          plot_flag = FALSE )

sim_cr
sim_cr %>% slice_max(ks_fisher_p_vals, n = 1)
```

We plot the three dimensional region via slices at the true parameter values using heatmaps for the p-values and with white background for the parameter values not included at the $\alpha = 0.05$ level.

```{r}
library(viridisLite)

alpha <- 0.05
rng <- range(sim_cr$ks_fisher_p_vals)
threshold_pos <- (alpha - rng[1]) / (rng[2] - rng[1])  # where alpha falls in [0,1]

n <- 256
viridis_cols <- viridis(n)

pval_scale <- scale_fill_gradientn(
  colours = c("white", "white", viridis_cols),
  values  = c(0, threshold_pos, seq(threshold_pos, 1, length.out = n)),
  limits  = rng
)
```

```{r}
df_slice1 <- sim_cr %>% filter(theta1 == 1)
df_slice2 <- sim_cr %>% filter(theta2 == 0)
df_slice3 <- sim_cr %>% filter(theta3 == 0)

p1 <- ggplot(df_slice1, aes(x = theta2, y = theta3, fill = ks_fisher_p_vals)) +
  geom_tile() +
  pval_scale +
  labs(title = expression(theta[1] == 1),
       x = expression(theta[2]), y = expression(theta[3]),
       fill = expression(italic(p)*"-value")) +
  theme_minimal()

p2 <- ggplot(df_slice2, aes(x = theta1, y = theta3, fill = ks_fisher_p_vals)) +
  geom_tile() +
  pval_scale +
  labs(title = expression(theta[2] == 0),
       x = expression(theta[1]), y = expression(theta[3]),
       fill = expression(italic(p)*"-value")) +
  theme_minimal()

p3 <- ggplot(df_slice3, aes(x = theta1, y = theta2, fill = ks_fisher_p_vals)) +
  geom_tile() +
  pval_scale +
  labs(title = expression(theta[3] == 0),
       x = expression(theta[1]), y = expression(theta[2]),
       fill = expression(italic(p)*"-value")) +
  theme_minimal()

(p1 + p2 + p3) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid = element_blank())
```
